shots.title: Classify gh lookup, authentication, timeout, exit, and buffer failures with bounded diagnostics (#590)

hazards.description: The first timeout implementation waited indefinitely if a child ignored termination, and the wrapper retained an unbounded legacy gh call.

shots.notes: The repaired transport drains bounded pipes, redacts credentials, reports typed failures and exit details, and guarantees terminal settlement after timeout escalation.

shots.title: Retrieve large PR metadata and diffs without the prior exec buffer ceiling (#590)

hazards.description: Initial paging used small pages without an aggregate deadline, and UTF-8 prefixing could become quadratic for multibyte patches.

shots.notes: The final collector uses 100-file pages, one 120-second collection deadline, strict metadata, linear byte-safe truncation, and an explicit 3,000-file ceiling warning.

shots.title: Add explicit include and exclude path filters for bounded review scope (#590)
shots.notes: Repeatable include/exclude globs match normalized current and previous rename paths and are forwarded strictly by slope pr review.

shots.title: Cover oversized diffs, filtered prompts, and provider-truncation messaging (#590)
shots.notes: Regressions cover output above 1 MiB, 3,000 files, ignored termination, multibyte budgets, dynamic fences, malformed metadata, and distinct provider/local coverage states.

conditions.description: Large provider output requires independent bounds on every process, page, aggregate collection, retained byte, and prompt boundary.

training.description: A timeout is not bounded unless termination and final settlement are bounded too.
training.outcome: The runner escalates termination and resolves terminally even if close never arrives.

training.description: Replacing one large command does not help if a wrapper keeps an older unbounded lookup.
training.outcome: The PR wrapper now reuses the single paginated provider result.

nutrition.description: Eighty-eight focused review-runner and wrapper tests passed after review repairs.
Production build and TypeScript typecheck passed for the completed S234 implementation.
Two independent reviews rejected the first pass; all seven findings were repaired and the final re-review approved.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: The happy-path collector was straightforward; proving that every failure and truncation path stayed bounded required the real work.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: Trace the complete wrapper-to-provider lifecycle and put independent bounds on process exit, pagination, retained data, and prompt encoding.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: A tiny UTF-8 helper and an advisory timeout could each defeat the entire large-diff design.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: Review prompts can now cover large PRs honestly without pretending omitted content was reviewed.

bunker_locations: A single legacy execSync in a wrapper can reintroduce the buffer and timeout failure the new collector removes.
Do not call a process timeout complete until close or a bounded terminal settlement has occurred.
Byte budgets must use linear, code-point-safe truncation for untrusted multibyte text.
yardage_book_updates: collectReviewDiff is the single bounded provider boundary for review-run and pr-review workflows.
course_management_notes: Implementation and independent review evidence are pushed; no PR merge or release is implied.
